prompts.excerpt: Strict keep rule: both judges must prefer the polish and neither may report a regression.

Camera/robot pose/geometry are locked; evaluate image fidelity, materials, illumination, readability and any regressions. Look closely, do not assume B is newer. Choose A, B, or TIE overall. List specific improvements and regressions of your winner, and the biggest remaining reference gaps.

lessons.title: A better vote is not an approval.
lessons.claim: None of five one-pass polish candidates cleared the two-reviewer non-regression rule. A current review composite is not a release.
lessons.tension: Small improvements can hide a new regression.
lessons.turn: Keep the merge when a vote ties or a regression appears.

source.label: Five-scene merge and polish review, October 14

lessons.title: Lock the element. Not the whole world.
lessons.claim: Day r90 locked the stair geometry while print placement, orb height and lighting remained open.
lessons.tension: A local success can become a false whole-scene sign-off.
lessons.turn: Name the exact object and properties that the owner accepted.

source.label: Day step geometry lock, r90

lessons.title: Match intent before pixels.
lessons.claim: Night changed from literal reference matching to per-element COPY and INTENT constraints, with component review before integration.
lessons.tension: A reference label copied onto different geometry can look wrong.
lessons.turn: Judge the brief and the owner locks, not resemblance alone.

source.label: Night v2 art-direction brief

lessons.title: Change the mechanism, not one more dial.
lessons.claim: The Night meta review identified repeated variants retaining the same blocker; its stop rule calls for two genuinely different directions after two focused failures.
lessons.tension: More hair curves or another brightness value need not change the visible form.
lessons.turn: Research the mechanism, prove a small coupon, then test on the frozen integrated fixture.

source.label: Night v2 meta review

lessons.title: Names are not evidence.
lessons.claim: Eye materials with clean-looking names still used photo-projection branches. Blue also had object-linked overrides. Verification inspected effective slots after reopening.
lessons.tension: A correct material name can conceal the wrong shader.
lessons.turn: Audit the rendered dependency graph and the saved scene, not only the script.

source.label: Permanent geometry-owned eye repair

lessons.title: Reproduce before taking credit.
lessons.claim: Blue changed strongly even in the fresh no-layer baseline. The carry-over report refuses to credit the layer for that baseline drift.
lessons.tension: A striking before/after can measure a renderer change rather than the intended edit.
lessons.turn: Use the same capture standard and a no-change control. Keep unlike judge contexts separate.
